messages:
Maya G: heads up, seeing a spike of correctable ECCs on pool-nyc-gpu-3, ~160/min over last 10m. dmesg shows repeated Xid 79 entries.
Oli: oof, are they spread across GPUs or single host?
Maya G: host gpu-07 shows majority. sample:
```
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off bus.
[12345.679012] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed!
```
Maya G: alert idea: prometheus rule using rate(node_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]) > 20 per host for 10m.
Sam: What's current auto-drain config? I thought we had drain-on-uncorrectable only.
Tess: correct — auto-drain only triggers for uncorrectable ECC / Xid fatals at the moment. correctables are manual triage.
Maya G: proposal: add sliding-window auto-action for correctables: if host-level rate > 50/min for 10m OR >100 correctables in 1h -> tag as `gpu:probation` and run cordon+evict (dry-run first).
Oli: +1 but add region-suppression: if >= 5 hosts in region show spikes, suppress auto-drain and open incident instead. avoids cascading capacity loss.
Sam: add a retry/backoff: cordon -> drain -> if eviction fails try once more after 5m, then create Jira and notify oncall.
infra-bot: note: firmware update scheduled for host gpu-07 at 1759001360 (vendor: nvidia, fw:v470.103).
Maya G: cost note: draining a host reduces pool capacity; expected p95 latency bump ~5% for our batch workload, but reduces risk of full uncorrectable later. tradeoffs documented.
Tess: playbook addition: if a serial has >2 auto-drains in 7d -> escalate to vendor RMA and mark device as replacement candidate.
Maya G: also add a quick-run checklist:
- run `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc`
- check `dmesg` for Xid patterns
- confirm model/driver/fw versions
- run `nvmlDeviceGetRetiredPages` check (or equivalent)
Oli: I'll draft the prometheus alert + grafana panel. Sam can wire the k8s drain job (with dry-run toggle).
Sam: creating infra PR for automation and runbook now, will include circuit-breaker config and region-suppression rule.
ops-bot: auto-drain dry-run scheduled at 1759001500 for pool-nyc-gpu-3 (no actual evictions).
Maya G: thanks — keep this thread for notes and postmortem items.
